liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls this Shakedown deeply funky; Reviewer considers it the best Shakedown ever, apart from a recording glitch in the first minute [12][14]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat into I Know You Rider is praised as rocking [17]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): The jam ending The Wheel is called among the best non-spaced-out jams, comparable to Playin' or Lonesome and a Long [19]
- **Spanish Jam** (1 review): Spanish Jam is called smoking, as are the jams around Never Trust A Woman [14]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Never Trust A Woman [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-08-28.mtx.painoman.92893.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 174 min; rated 4.27/5 by 11 [1]
- **gd1981-08-28.153337.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1981-08-28.fob.ellner.motb.91231.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 180 min; rated 4.11/5 by 9 [4]. Said about its sound: Large microphone taps at the starts of sets were edited out, while minor taps remain [4]
- **gd81-08-28.sbd-patched.painoman.9572.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 175 min; rated 4.71/5 by 21 [5]
- **gd1981-08-28.149185.FOB.Senn.Streeter.Miller.Noel.reMaster.t-flac2496**: source not stated; 22 songs; 180 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [7]
- **gd81-08-28.sbd.painoman.8670.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 167 min; rated 4.46/5 by 13 [10]. Said about its sound: Second set soundboard sounds hot; it was also issued on vinyl; The openings of Jack Straw and Shakedown Street are cut, and Never Trust a Woman has a cut [11][13]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls that in Las Vegas someone asked Brent in his hotel room the name of his song, Good Time Blues [15]
- Band members blow lyrics frequently and are all over the place, though The Wheel and Spanish Jam redeem it [17]
- Reviewer's first Dead show, held in the murky Long Beach Arena among a tie-dyed crowd; they knew only Skeletons from the Closet songs [21]
- From The Wheel through Wharf Rat the show is different and stronger than the rest [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-08-28.153337.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 304 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [2]. Also: Patches come from a Sennheiser 421 source (Never Trust A Woman) and a Nakamichi 700 source (Drums, Truckin' > Wharf Rat transition) [2]
- **gd1981-08-28.fob.ellner.motb.91231.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ron Ellner; transferred by MAC Supplied By: Barry Glassberg, Transfer by Adam Egert, Mastering by Bill Koucky; source: 2 x Nakamichi CM-700 => Sony TC-D5 >> MAC [4]. Also: Never Trust A Woman tape flip patched from the painoman 9572 source; crossfades cover first-set pauses and tape flips [4]
- **gd81-08-28.sbd-patched.painoman.9572.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]. Also: Most tapes of this show circulating come from the recording that was widely released on vinyl; The performance was released as a live LP; Soundboard transferred via CD with audience-source patches from cassette and DAT, seeded to etree by PainoMan in May 2002 [5][19][20]
- **gd1981-08-28.149185.FOB.Senn.Streeter.Miller.Noel.reMaster.t-flac2496**: taped by Master Cassette Recording by Frank Streeter; transferred by DSD Transfer by Charlie Miller;Edited & reMastered w/ Adobe Audition by Joe Noel; source: (FOB) Sennheiser 421 > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M) [7]
- **gd81-08-28.sbd.painoman.8670.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [10]. Also: Source has at least one analog generation, but tape hiss is minimal; A copy exists with the missing pieces patched in from an audience source, making it the complete show [12][18]
